medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Applications from students from groups under-represented in medicine are encouraged and will be given every consideration. All students are encouraged to take advantage of the services provided by the Office of Student and Community Engagement. These include a pre-matriculation program, an MCAT preparation course, and a summer research program for high school students, as well as informal counseling for medical students and applicants.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence may be granted by the Dean to a student who has no course grades of less than a "C," who is performing satisfactorily in ongoing courses, and who has no non-academic impediments. Leave may be taken for good cause, such as illness, extreme personal hardship, or other appropriate reasons. On rare occasions, the Dean may allow a leave of absence to a student who is performing poorly academically, when it appears that such performance may be related to illness, or other circumstances beyond the student's control. Under such circumstances, the Dean may stipulate that upon return to medical school, the student must maintain a specified level of academic performance or otherwise risk dismissal from medical school. Students taking a short-term leave of absence must make arrangements with the faculty involved for completion of course work and other assignments. medSchoolStudLife.setting: The medical school is located near the intersection of I-49 and I-20, in a peaceful neighborhood near the geographic center of Shreveport. Thus, safe, modern, affordable housing is available within a short commute.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing is not offered; however, safe, affordable housing is abundantly available within a short commuting distance.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Our Mission is to promote the health and wellness of LSU Health Shreveport through education and efforts that encourage habits of wellness, inspire and empower individuals to take responsibility for their own health, and support a sense of community in which health and overall well-being is recognized as an essential element of success.

Emotional, social, workplace and physical well-being are critical to the development and maintenance of competent, caring students, faculty and healthcare providers. In the current health care environment, students, residents, fellows, faculty members and staff are at increased risk for burnout and depression. Self-care is an important component that impacts qualify of life and work. It is also a skill that must be cultivated and developed.

https://www.lsuhs.edu/on-campus/institutional-wellness
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
In our School of Medicine, students develop meaningful relationships with faculty from day one as they are taught in the classroom and labs by the same doctors who will be teaching them in hospitals, clinics and research settings. These faculty members represent 18 clinical departments, which encompass over a dozen highly specialized divisions in addition to five basic science departments.

As a part of a new curriculum, students begin engaging with patients starting in their first year, further strengthening collaborative learning which is a hallmark of the new curriculum. The student experience is further enriched by standardized patient experiences and clinical skills training. Students also have the opportunity to complete a research distinction track.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Because on-campus housing is not available and very little off-campus housing is within walking distance, most students drive to school. Public transportation is available throughout most of the City however, transportation schedules are not guaranteed to be convenient.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional attire is expected at all times.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Peer tutoring is available through the Office of Student Affairs. The time requirements of research/patient care make it difficult to fix regular office hours; most faculty are available on request.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Extensive patient interaction is part of the required curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The modern, systems-based curriculum thoroughly integrates medical issues and applications in the first two years, during which the basic sciences are emphasized. Recently, didactic lecture hours were cut dramatically, and small-group, active-learning experiences were dramatically increased. The overall effect was decreased contact hours and increased self-directed learning. All essential basic-science concepts traditionally taught in the first two years are now integrated with clinical examples, clinical cases, and standardized patient experiences. The required clerkships occur in the third year, and the fourth year is devoted to electives.

There are seven core required clerkships that occur in the third year, as well, as the opportunity to participate in two clinical subspecialty third year electives. The clinical experiences are centered in our academic medical centers in Shreveport and Monroe. Fourth year is devoted to electives and sub-internships in preparation for residency training. Additionally, fourth year affords students the opportunity to engage in several visiting student learning opportunities of their choosing, at away institutions.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Because these change periodically, information concerning programs and initiatives in primary care should be discussed with the individual departments, whose contact information can be found on the medical center's website.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Medical students are encouraged, but not required, to do research.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Research opportunities are available, but not required.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: LSU Health Shreveport (LSUHS) provides education, research, patient care services, and community outreach. Educating health professionals and scientists at all levels, its major responsibility includes the advancement and dissemination of knowledge in medicine and the basic sciences. It also provides vital public service through its affiliated hospitals and clinics.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The primary mission of Louisiana State University Health Shreveport (LSUHS) is to teach, heal, and discover, in order to advance the wellbeing of the region and beyond. LSUHS comprises the Schools of Medicine, Graduate Studies, and Allied Health Professions in Shreveport. In implementing its mission, LSUHS is committed to:

- Educating physicians, scientists, and residents for healthcare service, teaching and research.
- Providing state-of-the-art clinical care, including tertiary services, to an enlarging and diverse regional base of patients.
- Achieving distinction and international recognition for basic science and clinical research programs that contribute to the practice in science and medicine.
- Supporting the region and the State in economic growth and prosperity by utilizing research and knowledge to engage in productive partnerships with the private sector.
- Fostering a culture that promotes mutual respect for all.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Accepted applicants must allow a criminal background check when requested.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: We use AMCAS Letters Service exclusively. Letters of Recommendation received via email, US Mail, or any method other than AMCAS Letters Service will not be made part of the official AMCAS application.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
While not required, we strongly prefer a letter from your Pre-professional Advisory Committee or its equivalent. If you have a Committee evaluation, you need no others. If your Committee sends a packet of letters without a consensus evaluation, then that packet should contain at least three signed, dated letters. If your school does not have a Committee, or should you fail to meet their requirements/deadlines, we advise you to get letters from three individual professors. Science professors are strongly preferred. Letters must be current - dated not earlier than May of your application year. 

If you completed your undergraduate degree more than two years ago, and have not been enrolled in a post-bacc or masters program, letters from immediate supervisors or military commanders (if applicable) will suffice.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two semi-blind, one-on-one interviews using structured and semi-structured question format. "Semi-blind" meaning interviewers will not have access to metrics, letters of recommendation, nor file updates prior to the interview.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews are held via virtual meeting platform.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: We admit out-of-state students who are US citizens or permanent residents.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
While coursework completed at the community or junior college is allowed, the Committee strongly prefers that courses are completed at a regionally accredited college or university. All coursework must be completed in the United States. In-person classes are strongly preferred, but not required. For Academic Years 2020 and 2021, we will allow both pass/fail grades and on-line courses for pre-requisites. 

All required coursework must be completed prior to matriculation. Applicants are responsible for ensuring that pre-requisite coursework is completed. 

Letters of Recommendation are required. We strongly prefer a letter from your Pre-professional Advisory Committee or its equivalent. If you have a Committee evaluation, you need no others. If your Committee sends a packet of letters without a consensus evaluation, then that packet should contain 3-5 signed, dated letters. If your school does not have a Committee, or should you fail to meet their requirements/deadlines, we advise you to get letters from three individual professors. Science professors are preferred.

Realize that letters from writers besides your Committee or professors usually provide limited useful information and therefore impact your competitive standing marginally, if at all.

We use the AMCAS Letters Service exclusively, and the only way to add your support to an applicant’s file is via AMCAS Letters Service. Email, US Mail, hand delivery, FedEx, phone calls, etc., will not work.

Applicants are responsible for ensuring that the appropriate letters are provided to AMCAS. Refer to AMCAS for detailed instructions.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Scholarships and long-term, low-interest loan funds are available to students with financial need. In the past, no accepted students have been unable to meet their financial needs. Scholarships and loans are available to students in all four years and are based on applicants' showing verified need. Certain awards are given in recognition primarily of academic accomplishment and promise. The school offers summer employment to many students, but does not advise employment during school sessions, which would interfere with academic performance. Financial need has no bearing on an applicant's acceptance.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The MD-PhD Program promotes the education of physician scientists through dual enrollment in the School of Graduate Studies and the School of Medicine at LSU Health Shreveport in a more efficient and productive sequence than could be otherwise accomplished. The integration of clinical studies and research throughout the program is designed to encourage graduates to pursue research and education in a clinical setting throughout their careers.

Students enter medical school in August and complete 18 months of preclinical course work, ending in April of their second year of medical school. The USMLE STEP 1 Exam is taken in May or June, followed by the third year of medical school (clinical clerkships).

After completion of the USMLE STEP 2 Exam, students matriculate into the School of Graduate Studies to conduct their PhD research.

Following successful defense of their PhD dissertation, students return to the clinic to complete their final year of clerkships.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The following courses are required:
English - 6 semester hours
Chemistry - 12 semester hours (must include at least 3 Biochemistry lecture hours)
Biological Sciences - 12 semester hours
Humanities - 12 semester hours (in addition to the English requirement)
Total must be at least 90 semester hours.
medSchoolSelection.premedCourseworkNote: Note: This School has progressed to a competency-based admissions process.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We do not require that coursework be completed within a specific timeframe. It is up to the applicant to decide if older coursework will prepare him for the rigor of medical school.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Admission is based upon character, motivation, intellectual ability, and achievement as judged by recommendations of premedical advisors, personal interviews with members of the Admissions Committee at the School of Medicine, college grades, and MCAT scores. In recent years, the number of applications filed by well-qualified residents of Louisiana has far exceeded the number of places available. For this reason, a limited number of places have been offered to nonresidents. State of Legal Residence is determined by LSU system regulations. The School of Medicine in Shreveport does not discriminate in applicant selection on the basis of race, sex, creed, national origin, age, nor handicap.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We do not recommend specific numbers of shadowing hours. Nor do we have a minimum required number. Many successful applicants have amassed hundreds of hours; many others significantly less than that.
